Notebook introduction

This document provides an in-depth architectural breakdown, implementation analysis, and complete developer manual for [Instanced](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/Instanced.ts), [Arrange](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/layout/Arrange.ts), CPU vs. GPU instancing modes, and real-time **WebGPU Compute Shader** integration in the Retiam Engine.
1. Architectural Overview & Design Philosophy

Retiam is designed to bridge declarative motion-graphics workflows (similar to Manim or Motion Canvas) with extreme real-time WebGPU performance (10,000 to 100,000+ interactive instances at 60–120 FPS).
The Three Core Components

items: **[Instanced](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/Instanced.ts)**:

blocks.text: A low-level, high-performance rendering entity that executes single-draw-call hardware instancing via **programmable vertex-pulling from a WebGPU storage buffer** (`GPUBufferUsage.STORAGE | GPUBufferUsage.COPY_DST`).

items: **[Arrange](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/layout/Arrange.ts)**:

blocks.text: A high-level procedural layout container. It replicates a template entity across 1D linear lines, 2D grids, 3D volume lattices, radial circles/arcs, and parametric curves. It operates in either **CPU Scene-Graph Mode** (`gpu: false`) or **GPU Instancing Mode** (`gpu: true`).

items: **WebGPU Compute Shader Integration**:

blocks.text: A direct pipeline connecting [ComputeKernel](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/compute/ComputeKernel.ts) to the [Instanced](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/Instanced.ts) storage buffer. Instead of running heavy JavaScript loops on the CPU and uploading megabytes across PCIe each frame, a compute shader mutates positions, scales, rotations, and colors **directly in GPU VRAM** in $<0.15\text{ ms}$.

blocks.text: 2. The Instanced Engine Entity Architecture
2.1 Programmable Vertex Pulling vs. Vertex Buffers

Traditional graphics APIs use per-instance vertex buffer attributes (`stepMode: 'instance'`). In WebGPU, this approach introduces rigid bind group layouts and prevents compute shaders from mutating instance data in place.
Retiam utilizes **programmable vertex-pulling**:

items: Per-instance transforms and colors reside in a **WebGPU Storage Buffer** (`array<vec4f>` or `array<Instance>`).
The vertex shader pulls instance parameters branchlessly using the WebGPU built-in `instance_index`.
Fragment shaders automatically receive the instance tint (`iColor`) via the varying schema.

blocks.text: 2.2 Storage Buffer Memory Layouts
[Instanced](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/Instanced.ts) supports two memory layout modes:

cells.text: Translation $(x,y,z)$, Uniform Scale $(s)$, RGBA Color, Quaternion $(qx,qy,qz,qw)$
Uniform particles, dots, circles, text glyphs
All standard fields + Independent 3D Scale $(sx, sy, sz)$ + Custom ID/UV tile

blocks.text: Memory Layout Diagram (Extended Mode — 16 Floats / 64 Bytes):

blocks.content: In WebGPU `std430` storage buffer layout rules, each `vec4f` has a 16-byte alignment and 16-byte size. Because 64 bytes is an exact multiple of 16, this maps **1:1 without padding hazards** to the WGSL `struct Instance`.

blocks.text: 2.3 Buffer Lifecycle & Partial Streaming
[Instanced](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/Instanced.ts) implements an intelligent partial streaming mechanism:

items: **`ensureGPUBuffer(device)`**: Guarantees the GPU buffer is allocated with `STORAGE | COPY_DST`. If `instanceCount` expands beyond buffer capacity, the buffer is reallocated and compute bindings are automatically rebuilt via `computeKernel.setResource(...)`.

**Dirty Range Tracking**: When CPU modifications occur (via `setInstancePosition`, `setInstanceColor`, etc.), `markDirty(index)` tracks `dirtyMinIndex` and `dirtyMaxIndex`. `prepare()` uploads **only the modified byte slice** to VRAM via `scene.device.queue.writeBuffer(...)`.

**Compute Pass Safety**: When a compute shader drives instance motion, `isDirty` remains `false`. As a result, the CPU performs **zero writeBuffer operations**, ensuring VRAM data is never clobbered by stale CPU arrays.

blocks.text: 2.4 Zero-Allocation 3D Raycasting & Picking ([IRaycastable](../src/engine/core/Interfaces.ts))
[Instanced](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/Instanced.ts) implements high-speed CPU raycasting over thousands of instances:

items: Uses static pre-allocated scratch vectors (`_scratchLocalOrigin`, `_scratchRelOrigin`, `_scratchQuatInv`).
Converts the world-space ray into each instance's local coordinate frame via inverse quaternion rotation and scale normalization.
Performs an analytical bounding sphere or template raycast test.
Returns the exact `instanceId` and hit coordinates.

[Arrange](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/layout/Arrange.ts) is Retiam's procedural layout engine. It takes a blueprint template entity and replicates it across mathematical distributions.

4. WebGPU Compute Shader Integration Architecture
4.1 The Scaling Problem with CPU Updaters
While GPU instancing solves the rendering bottleneck (1 draw call), dynamic animations traditionally required looping over instances on the CPU:

items: **CPU Cost**: $65,536 \times 60 = 3.93\text{ million}$ JavaScript iterations per second.
**PCIe Cost**: $65,536 \times 64\text{ bytes} \times 60\text{ fps} \approx 251\text{ MB/s}$ continuous bandwidth saturation.
**Result**: Frame rates drop to 15–20 FPS on high-density grids.

blocks.text: 4.2 The Solution: WebGPU Compute Shaders

By connecting [ComputeKernel](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/compute/ComputeKernel.ts) directly to `Instanced.instanceBuffer`, instance transformations are calculated **in-place in GPU VRAM**:

items: **Execution Cost**: $<0.15\text{ ms}$ on the GPU via parallel workgroups.
**CPU Cost**: **0%** (CPU simply queues an $O(1)$ dispatch command).
**PCIe Cost**: **0 MB/s** (data never leaves VRAM).

4.4 Frame-by-Frame Execution Lifecycle

blocks.code:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant App as Scene Loop (CPU)
    participant Inst as Arrange / Instanced
    participant Kernel as ComputeKernel
    participant Pass as FrameGraph (ComputeUpdate)
    participant GPU as WebGPU Device (VRAM)
    participant Render as Render Pass

    App->>Inst: update(time, dt)
    Inst->>Inst: dispatchCompute(time, dt)
    Inst->>GPU: queue.writeBuffer(uniformBuffer, {time, dt, count})
    Inst->>Kernel: dispatch(device, workgroups)
    Kernel->>App: scene.addCompute(command)
    App->>Pass: execute(RenderContext)
    Pass->>GPU: beginComputePass() -> dispatchWorkgroups()
    Note over GPU: Compute Shader mutates instanceBuffer in VRAM (<0.15ms)
    Pass->>GPU: end()
    App->>Render: Forward / Shadow Render Passes
    Note over GPU: Vertex Shader pulls updated positions directly from instanceBuffer
    Render->>GPU: Draw 1 Call to Screen

blocks.text: 5. API Reference & Method Signatures
5.1 Instanced
ensureGPUBuffer(device: GPUDevice): GPUBuffer
Allocates or validates the underlying GPU storage buffer. Reallocates and refreshes compute bindings if capacity needs to grow.
compute(computeLogicOrKernel: string | ComputeKernel, options?: InstancedComputeOptions): this
Attaches a compute shader or pre-compiled [ComputeKernel](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/compute/ComputeKernel.ts).

items: `computeLogicOrKernel`: WGSL logic snippet, full `@compute` WGSL module, or [ComputeKernel](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/compute/ComputeKernel.ts) instance.
`options.workgroupSize`: Thread dimensions `[X, Y, Z]` (defaults to `[64, 1, 1]`).
`options.extraResources`: Additional storage/uniform buffers or textures.
`options.autoDispatch`: Whether to automatically dispatch every frame (defaults to `true`).

blocks.text: dispatchCompute(time?: number, dt?: number): void
Uploads latest `{ time, dt, count }` to the uniform buffer and submits the compute command to `scene.addCompute(...)`.
5.2 Arrange
onCompute(wgslLogicOrKernel: string | ComputeKernel, options?: InstancedComputeOptions): this

Fluent chaining method. Wires compute shaders directly to the internal [Instanced](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/Instanced.ts) node when `{ gpu: true }` is enabled.
onUpdate(fn: (time: number, dt: number, arrange: this) => void): this
Attaches a CPU-side frame updater callback (automatically syncs to GPU buffer via `syncGPU()`).
setCount(newCount: number): this
Dynamically expands or shrinks instance count. Handles GPU buffer expansion and proxy entity pooling.

7. Performance Best Practices & Gotchas
1. Always Guard Bounds in Compute Shaders

WebGPU dispatches workgroups in multiples of the workgroup size (e.g. 64 threads). If your instance count is 100,000, WebGPU dispatches $\lceil 100,000 / 64 \rceil = 1,563$ workgroups $= 100,032$ threads. Always include:

blocks.code:
let i = id.x;
if (i >= uniforms.count) { return; }

blocks.text: *(When passing raw snippets without `@compute`, `Instanced.compute()` automatically prepends this safeguard).*
2. Time Scale

In Retiam, `scene.time` is recorded in milliseconds. Therefore, `uniforms.time` passed to compute shaders increases by $\approx 1000$ per second. To achieve normal mathematical wave speeds in your shader, multiply by `0.001`:
3. CPU vs. GPU State Divergence
When compute shaders mutate `instances[i].pos_scale`, the changes occur **in GPU VRAM only**. The CPU-side `instanceData` `Float32Array` remains in its base state.

items: For visual motion graphics, this is optimal (maximum speed, 0 PCIe readback).
If your application requires precise CPU raycasting or physics collisions on compute-driven positions, test against the initial layout boundaries or perform asynchronous readbacks.
